issues.legal_issue: A statutory tenant whose contractual tenancy has ended may grant a valid licence while remaining in possession under statutory protection and before an eviction decree is passed.
material_facts: The original tenant's contractual tenancy had been terminated, but he remained in possession under the protection of rent-control law.
Before his death, he granted two occupants a licence to use part of the premises.
No eviction decree had been passed against him when he granted the licence.
issues.conclusion: The licence was legally valid notwithstanding the termination of the contractual tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory tenant who continues in occupation under rent-control protection and against whom no eviction decree has been passed can create a licence. The Court relied on Chandavarkar Sita Ratna Rao v. Ashalata S. Guram.

rule.if: license_creation_dispute and statutory_tenant_remained_in_possession and no_eviction_decree and license_granted

predicates.license_creation_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a person who granted permission to occupy premises created a valid licence.
predicates.statutory_tenant_remained_in_possession: A tenant whose contractual tenancy had ended continued in possession under statutory protection.
predicates.no_eviction_decree: No decree for eviction had been passed against the tenant when permission to occupy was granted.
predicates.license_granted: The tenant gave another person permission to occupy premises under a licence arrangement.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns a licence granted by a tenant who remains in protected possession and has not been evicted by decree, the licence is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A licensee occupying premises under a valid and continuing licence on the legally specified qualifying day acquires deemed-tenant protection.
material_facts: The occupants received a valid licence to occupy part of the premises.
Evidence included correspondence from the tenant's heirs continuing the arrangement and seeking compensation, as well as an earlier declaratory decree in favour of an occupant.
The appellate court found that the licence continued on the qualifying day, and the Supreme Court found material supporting that conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The occupants were entitled to deemed-tenant protection for the licensed portion of the premises.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 15A and 5(4A) of the Bombay Rent Act, a person had to be in occupation as a licensee under a subsisting licence on the specified day. The Court relied on D.H. Maniar v. Waman Laxman Kudav, Ludhichem Agencies v. Ahmed R.V. Peer Mohamed, and Chandavarkar Sita Ratna Rao v. Ashalata S. Guram.

predicates.deemed_tenancy_claim: An occupant claims statutory recognition as a tenant based on occupation under a licence.
predicates.license_is_valid: The permission to occupy was granted under a legally valid licence.
predicates.license_continued_on_qualifying_day: The licence remained in force and the occupant remained in occupation on the legally specified qualifying day.

issues.definition: A valid licensee who remains in occupation under a continuing licence on the qualifying day acquires deemed-tenant status when claiming that statutory protection.

issues.legal_issue: A supervisory court may not set aside a lower court's factual finding unless the finding lacks evidentiary support or is perverse.
material_facts: The appellate court found that the licence continued after the original tenant's death and remained in force on the qualifying day.
Correspondence and other material supported the finding that the arrangement continued.
The High Court, exercising supervisory jurisdiction, set aside that factual finding based on the licence's stated expiry date.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in setting aside the appellate court's finding because the finding had evidentiary support and was not shown to be perverse.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 227 of the Constitution, a High Court may interfere with a factual finding only where there is no evidence to support it or where no reasonable person could have reached it; otherwise, it cannot reweigh the facts. The Court relied on Chandavarkar Sita Ratna Rao v. Ashalata S. Guram.

predicates.supervisory_review_of_factual_finding: A court exercising supervisory jurisdiction reviews a factual finding made by a lower court or tribunal.
predicates.evidence_supports_finding: Evidence in the record supports the lower court's factual finding.
predicates.finding_not_perverse: The finding is one that a reasonable decision-maker could reach on the evidence.

issues.definition: On supervisory review, a supported and non-perverse factual finding must not be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An eviction order against a tenant's heirs cannot be used to evict deemed tenants from the portion they occupy under a protected licence.
material_facts: The occupants were not parties to the landlords' eviction proceeding against the tenant's heirs.
The occupants' licence covered only part of the premises, and they were entitled to deemed-tenant protection for that part.
The landlords sought to execute the order against the occupants, while the occupants objected to their removal from the licensed portion.
issues.conclusion: The occupants could not be evicted from the licensed portion on the basis of the order against the heirs; eviction from that portion had to proceed under the applicable rent-control law.
issues.legal_principle: A deemed tenant protected under Section 15A of the Bombay Rent Act could be evicted only in accordance with that Act, not by executing an order made against other persons. The protection extended only to the portion covered by the licence.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and occupant_acquired_deemed_tenancy and premises_part_covered_by_license and order_was_against_other_occupants

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A person in possession objects in execution proceedings to being removed under an order for possession.
predicates.occupant_acquired_deemed_tenancy: The occupant acquired statutory tenant status based on occupation under a qualifying licence.
predicates.premises_part_covered_by_license: The portion from which removal is sought was covered by the occupant's licence.
predicates.order_was_against_other_occupants: The possession order was made against persons other than the occupant objecting to execution.

issues.definition: In an execution objection, a deemed tenant cannot be removed from the portion covered by the licence under an order made against other occupants.

issues.legal_issue: A possession order is not a nullity merely because the occupants raise a defence to the original claim, and it may be enforced against the parties bound by it for property outside the protected licensed portion.
material_facts: The landlords' eviction application alleged that the tenant's statutory tenancy ended on his death and that his heirs had no right to remain in possession.
The heirs claimed tenancy in their written statement but did not pursue that claim, and the order was made against them.
The heirs did not challenge the order and later disclaimed an interest in the premises.
The portion outside the licence was not protected by the occupants' deemed-tenancy status.
issues.conclusion: The order was not without jurisdiction as against the heirs and could be enforced for the portion outside the licence; the landlords were entitled to possession of that remainder.
issues.legal_principle: Jurisdiction is determined by the averments in the plaint or claim application, not by the opposing party's defence. If the alleged jurisdictional facts are not established, the proceeding is dismissed for failure to prove them. The Court relied on Sanwarmal Kejriwal v. Vishwa Cooperative Housing Society Ltd. and, on the general effect of a jurisdictional defect, Kiran Singh v. Chaman Paswan.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and original_claim_alleged_facts_supporting_jurisdiction and order_was_against_bound_parties and property_part_outside_protected_licence

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A person objects during execution of an order for possession.
predicates.original_claim_alleged_facts_supporting_: The original claim alleged facts which, if established, gave the court authority to hear the proceeding.
predicates.order_was_against_bound_parties: The order was made against parties who are bound by it and who have not successfully challenged it.
predicates.property_part_outside_protected_licence: The property sought to be recovered is outside the portion protected by the occupant's licence.

issues.definition: In an execution objection, an order based on jurisdiction-supporting allegations remains enforceable against bound parties for property outside a protected licensed portion.

issues.legal_issue: Licensees who continue to occupy premises must pay compensation for their use and occupation to the owners entitled to receive it.
material_facts: The occupants had paid compensation for the initial licence period and deposited an additional sum with the original tenant.
They did not claim to have paid further compensation for their continued occupation.
The tenant's heirs disclaimed any interest in the premises, and the owners remained entitled to the compensation.
issues.conclusion: The occupants were liable to pay compensation to the owners for their use and occupation, with the amounts already paid credited against their liability and further payments made as directed by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed payment of compensation for use and occupation to the owners because the occupants continued in possession and the former tenant's heirs claimed no interest in the premises.

predicates.occupants_remained_in_possession: The licensees continued to occupy the premises after the initial licence period.
predicates.owners_entitled_to_compensation: The owners were entitled to receive compensation for the occupants' use and occupation.
predicates.prior_payments_made_to_former_tenant: The occupants had paid an amount to the former tenant for the initial period of occupation.

issues.definition: Occupants who remain in possession must pay compensation to the owners entitled to receive it, with prior payments to the former tenant taken into account.
